phenotype_specificity.statement: P63 (PMID 33391282) is in the mild LAD1^+ class (CD18 ≥30%) and had no recorded delayed cord separation; the paper describes the hallmark features of the disease in general terms. No other genes were reported as tested for LAD1 patients (Sanger sequencing of ITGB2). A0111 has no clinical data.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Batch HGVS: canonical splice-acceptor change at intron 12 position -2; predicted p.?. PMID 22134107 proposes "Deletion exon 13? p.Gly553AlafsX6" with a question mark; PMID 33391282 gives "IVS12-2". The paper describes the disease as caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (the β2 integrin subunit).

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.

concerns: PMID 22134107 is a mutation-update table (Table I) without case descriptions: people are identified only by database accession numbers, and sex, age and clinical features are not given per person.

In Table I the LAD-I type and the families (alleles) count belong to the table row (the variant), not to one accession number; for an accession number listed with a second variant, the expression class reflects the person's genotype, not this allele alone.
Protein differs from the batch prediction: PMID 22134107 proposes "Deletion exon 13? p.Gly553AlafsX6" (tentative); the batch predicts p.?. No RNA study is described in either paper.

P63 zygosity is inconsistent in PMID 33391282 Table S2: c.751G>A is marked heterozygous (#) for P63, but c.1658-2A>G has no # for P63, so the table could be read as homozygous for c.1658-2A>G plus a third allele. Most likely a missing mark, but the paper does not say.

A0111 (22134107) and P63 (33391282) have different second alleles (c.809C>T vs c.751G>A), so they are probably different people; Dr Madkaikar is an author of both papers, and A0111 was unpublished in 2011.

PMID 22134107 also lists a separate row with an unidentified nucleotide change giving the same predicted consequence (deletion exon 13, p.Gly553AlafsX6), references [3, 38]; that row is not this variant as written.
P63's phenotype class LAD1^+ (CD18 ≥30%) is the mild class; the PMID 33391282 Table S1 supplement is truncated in the converted text, but the P63 row is present.
P63 has a second candidate variant in ITGB2 (c.751G>A, p.Gly251Ser), which the same table lists with an rs number.
notes_for_panel: Two carriers in two papers, each with a different second ITGB2 variant. The unidentified-nucleotide row in 22134107 with the same predicted exon 13 deletion is shown for context only.
